reading.title: Ancient Roman Architecture and Structural Innovation
reading.passage: Roman architecture represents one of history's most significant technological achievements, fundamentally transforming how civilizations construct buildings and infrastructure. The Romans pioneered the widespread use of concrete, known as opus caementicium, which revolutionized construction methods by enabling the creation of larger, more durable structures than previously possible. This innovation allowed architects to design ambitious projects such as the Pantheon, whose massive dome remained the world's largest unreinforced concrete structure for nearly two thousand years. Beyond concrete, Roman engineers developed the arch and vault systems, which distributed weight more efficiently than earlier post-and-lintel construction techniques, allowing for taller buildings and longer spans. These structural innovations were not merely aesthetic achievements; they had profound practical implications for society. The aqueducts that transported fresh water across vast distances relied on arched construction, while amphitheaters could accommodate tens of thousands of spectators safely. Subsequently, Roman architectural principles influenced building design throughout Europe during the Renaissance and remain relevant to modern engineering. Contemporary architects continue to study Roman structures to understand principles of durability, efficiency, and sustainable design that have proven effective over millennia.

vocabulary.meaning_ko: 로마 시대의 콘크리트, 고대 로마 건축에 사용된 시멘트 혼합물

questions.q: According to the passage, what was the primary advantage of Roman concrete over earlier building materials?
options: It was more affordable to produce on a large scale
It enabled the construction of larger and more durable structures
It required less skilled labor to apply properly
It was more visually appealing in appearance
questions.explanation: 지문의 두 번째 문장에서 'revolutionized construction methods by enabling the creation of larger, more durable structures than previously possible'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about the Pantheon's dome?
options: It was the first concrete structure ever built by Romans
It required reinforcement to remain standing for two thousand years
Its structural design demonstrated the durability of Roman concrete
It was primarily built for religious rather than practical purposes
questions.explanation: 지문에서 Pantheon의 돔이 'nearly two thousand years' 동안 'unreinforced concrete' 구조로 남아있었다는 것은 로마 콘크리트의 내구성을 입증합니다.

questions.q: The word 'distributed' in the third sentence is closest in meaning to:
options: transported from one location to another
divided and spread throughout a structure
determined based on calculations
reduced through careful planning
questions.explanation: 'distributed weight'는 '무게를 구조 전체에 나누어 분산시킨다'는 의미이므로, '나누어 퍼지게 하다'가 가장 가까운 뜻입니다.

questions.q: Why does the author mention aqueducts and amphitheaters?
options: To explain why Romans preferred concrete over other materials
To provide examples of how structural innovations had practical applications
To argue that Roman engineering was superior to modern techniques
To demonstrate that Roman buildings were primarily for entertainment
questions.explanation: 저자는 이 예시들을 통해 로마의 구조적 혁신이 '실질적인 함의를 가졌다'는 주장을 뒷받침하고 있습니다.

model_sentences: The expansion of online education has fundamentally transformed how students access learning opportunities in the twenty-first century.

Online platforms provide unprecedented flexibility, allowing learners to study at their own pace and from any location, which is particularly beneficial for working professionals and students in remote areas.
For instance, a student in a rural community can now access world-class instruction from leading universities without relocating, thereby democratizing educational access.
However, online education also presents significant challenges, including reduced face-to-face interaction and the digital divide that disadvantages students without reliable internet connections.
Despite these drawbacks, the benefits of accessibility and flexibility suggest that online education will continue to play an increasingly important role alongside traditional classroom instruction.
Universities should therefore invest in improving the quality of online platforms while simultaneously addressing the technological and social barriers that prevent equitable access.
Ultimately, a blended approach combining both online and in-person learning offers the most promising path forward for educational institutions in the modern era.

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer reading books to learn about stories and ideas. Others prefer watching movies. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details in your response.
model_sentences: Personally, I prefer reading books over watching movies because books offer a deeper and more immersive experience.
When you read a novel, you actively engage your imagination to visualize characters, settings, and scenarios, which creates a more personal connection to the story.
For example, when I read 'The Lord of the Rings,' I could imagine Middle-earth according to my own vision, whereas a movie presents a fixed interpretation that everyone sees identically.
Additionally, books provide more detailed character development and internal thoughts that movies often have to cut or simplify due to time constraints.
While movies can be entertaining and visually stunning, I believe that the interactive nature of reading makes it a superior medium for truly understanding complex ideas and narratives.
Therefore, whenever I have the choice between reading a book and watching its film adaptation, I almost always choose the book first.

listening.title: Professor's Office Meeting About Research Paper Topic
listening.script:
Student: Professor Martinez, I wanted to discuss potential topics for my research paper. I'm thinking about studying the impact of sustainable architecture on urban development, but I'm not sure if it's too broad.

Professor: That's an excellent starting point. Sustainable architecture is definitely relevant, but you're right—it's quite expansive. Let me suggest a more focused approach. What if you narrowed it down to examine how green building certifications, like LEED, have influenced commercial real estate decisions in major cities over the past decade?

Student: That sounds much more manageable. Would I need to include case studies of specific buildings?

Professor: Absolutely. Case studies would strengthen your argument considerably. I'd recommend selecting three to four prominent LEED-certified buildings in different cities—perhaps New York, Los Angeles, and Singapore—and analyzing how their design choices addressed both environmental concerns and economic feasibility.

Student: What about the timeline? How far back should I research?

Professor: I'd suggest starting from 2010, when LEED certification became more standardized internationally. That gives you a solid fifteen-year window of data. Also, try to incorporate interviews or statements from architects if possible.

Student: This is really helpful. When should I have a draft completed?

Professor: Bring me a preliminary outline by next month. That way, we can make sure you're on the right track before you dive too deeply into research.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this conversation?
options: To explain the history of sustainable architecture
To help the student narrow down and refine a research paper topic
To discuss the professor's own research on green buildings
To encourage the student to study international architecture exclusively
questions.explanation: 교수가 학생의 광범위한 주제를 좀 더 구체적으로 좁히는 것을 돕기 위해 제안하고 조언합니다.

questions.q: What does the professor recommend the student do to strengthen the research paper?
options: Focus only on European LEED-certified buildings
Include case studies of three to four prominent buildings in different cities
Research only buildings constructed after 2015
Interview only architects from North America
questions.explanation: 교수는 '케이스 스터디가 당신의 주장을 상당히 강화할 것'이라고 말하며, 다양한 도시의 3-4개 건물을 선택할 것을 권장합니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor suggest starting research from 2010?
options: Because that is when LEED certification was first invented
Because that year marked the beginning of sustainable architecture
Because LEED certification became more standardized internationally around that time
Because most of the world's major cities were built in 2010
questions.explanation: 교수는 '2010년은 LEED 인증이 국제적으로 더 표준화되었을 때'라고 명확히 설명합니다.
